```{r}
# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(sf)

# Just trying to convert Date format for ease of processing later
ohio_accidents$Date <- dmy(ohio_accidents$Date)

# I am cleaning the data by removing occurences with invalid or missing coordinates
ohio_accidents_clean <- ohio_accidents %>%
  dplyr::filter(Longitude < 0) %>%  # Trying to get rid of positive longitudes (should be negative in US)
  dplyr::filter(Longitude > -85 & Longitude < -80) %>%  # Adding Ohio longitude range
  dplyr::filter(Latitude > 38 & Latitude < 42)  # Adding latitude range then

nrow(ohio_accidents_clean)

# Then moving to conversion to sf object
ohio_accidents_sf <- st_as_sf(
  ohio_accidents_clean, 
  coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),
  crs = 4326  # WGS84 coordinate system
)

head(ohio_accidents_sf)

# Load necessary libraries
library(sf)
library(mapsf)

# First, let's transform our data to a geographic CRS (WGS84) for lat/long display
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)

# Set up the plotting area
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA, 
     border = NA,
     axes = FALSE,  # Turn off automatic axes
     main = "Pipeline Accidents in Ohio")

# Get the bounding box for grid lines
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)

# Create latitude and longitude breaks
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels nicely (degrees symbol)
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 2), "° W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Now add Ohio boundary
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo), 
     col = "white", 
     border = "black",
     add = TRUE)

# Add accident points
plot(st_geometry(ohio_accidents_geo), 
     col = "red", 
     pch = 16, 
     cex = 0.8,
     add = TRUE)

# Add manual axes with latitude/longitude labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# 5) Scale bar
mf_scale(
  pos = "bottomleft"
)


# Add box around the plot area
box()

```

```{r}
# Point Pattern Analysis
library(spatstat)

# I am creating a spatial window for point pattern analysis using Ohio boundary
ohio_win <- as.owin(st_geometry(ohio_boundary))

# then converting Ohio accident points to ppp format
ohio_pts <- st_coordinates(ohio_accidents_sf)
ohio_ppp <- ppp(ohio_pts[,1], ohio_pts[,2], window = ohio_win)

# then conducting a test for Complete Spatial Randomness (CSR)
# Nearest Neighbor Analysis
nn_test <- clarkevans.test(ohio_ppp)
print(nn_test)

# I am implementing Ripley's K function to check clustering at multiple distances
k_ohio <- Kest(ohio_ppp, correction = "border")
plot(k_ohio, main="Ripley's K Function: Ohio Pipeline Accidents")

# Then  doing a Kernel Density Estimation
ohio_density <- density.ppp(ohio_ppp, sigma = 10000)  # 10km bandwidth

library(sf)
library(spatstat)   # for ppp & density.ppp
library(sp)         # for CRS()/proj4string()
library(terra)      # for SpatRaster
library(mapsf)      # for the mapping functions
library(raster)     # for raster operations

# 1) build the point pattern & 5 km KDE in UTM --------------------------------
ohio_utm     <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 26917)
ohio_acc_utm <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 26917)
ohio_win <- as.owin(st_geometry(ohio_utm))
coords   <- st_coordinates(ohio_acc_utm)
suppressWarnings({
  ohio_ppp <- ppp(coords[,1], coords[,2], window = ohio_win, check = FALSE)
})
ohio_density <- density.ppp(ohio_ppp, sigma = 5000, edge = TRUE)

# 2) get back to geographic for sf plotting ----------------------------------
ohio_bound_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
ohio_acc_geo   <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)

# 3) convert the KDE ("im" object) into a terra SpatRaster -------------------
sgdf <- as(ohio_density, "SpatialGridDataFrame")
proj4string(sgdf) <- st_crs(26917)$proj4string   # tell it "this is UTM"

# Convert to a raster object (raster package) for better control
r <- raster(sgdf)

# Apply log transformation to match the reference map
r_log <- calc(r, fun = function(x) log10(x * 100 + 1))

# Project to WGS84
r_wgs84 <- projectRaster(r_log, crs = st_crs(4326)$proj4string)

# Create a mask from Ohio to constrain the KDE display
ohio_sp <- as(ohio_bound_geo, "Spatial")
r_masked <- mask(r_wgs84, ohio_sp)

# 4) colour ramp --------------------------------------------------------------
density_cols <- colorRampPalette(
  c("navy", "blue", "purple", "red", "orange", "yellow")
)(100)

# 5) draw the map with base R for better control -----------------------------
# Set margins to match reference
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 6))  # room for right-hand legend & title

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_bound_geo),
     col = NA, 
     border = NA,
     axes = FALSE,
     main = "")

# Get the bounding box for grid lines
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_bound_geo)

# Create latitude and longitude breaks
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 1), "°W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 1), "°N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}
for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Fill Ohio with white as the base layer
plot(st_geometry(ohio_bound_geo),
     col = "white",
     border = NA,
     add = TRUE)

# Plot the masked raster directly - the simpler approach that works
plot(r_masked, 
     col = density_cols, 
     add = TRUE, 
     legend = FALSE)

# Add Ohio boundary again with a clean black line
plot(st_geometry(ohio_bound_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "black",
     lwd = 1,
     add = TRUE)

# Add accident points
plot(st_geometry(ohio_acc_geo),
     col = "red",
     pch = 16,
     cex = 0.7,
     add = TRUE)

# Add title and subtitle separately for better control
title("Kernel Density of Pipeline Accidents in Ohio", cex.main = 1.2)
mtext("Smoothed with 5km Gaussian Kernel (log scale)", 
      side = 3, line = -0.1, cex = 0.8)

# Add axes with lat/long labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow (using mapsf)
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# Add scale bar (using mapsf)
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the plot area
box()

# Create the tick-style legend
par(xpd = TRUE)  # Allow plotting outside the plot region

# Calculate legend position based on the plot dimensions
usr <- par("usr")  # Get the plot region coordinates
legend_x <- usr[2] + 0.05 * (usr[2] - usr[1])
legend_y_bottom <- usr[3] + 0.25 * (usr[4] - usr[3])
legend_y_top <- usr[3] + 0.75 * (usr[4] - usr[3])
legend_width <- 0.02 * (usr[2] - usr[1])

# Draw the legend color bar
y_positions <- seq(legend_y_bottom, legend_y_top, length.out = 101)
for (i in 1:100) {
  rect(legend_x, y_positions[i], legend_x + legend_width, y_positions[i+1],
       col = density_cols[i], border = NA)
}

# Add a border around the color bar
rect(legend_x, legend_y_bottom, legend_x + legend_width, legend_y_top, 
     col = NULL, border = "black")

# Create custom legend labels
tick_positions <- seq(legend_y_bottom, legend_y_top, length.out = 5)
tick_labels <- c("0.0", "", "0.1", "", "0.3")  # Values from the reference image

# Draw tick marks and labels
segments(legend_x + legend_width, tick_positions, 
         legend_x + legend_width + 0.01 * (usr[2] - usr[1]), tick_positions)
text(legend_x + legend_width + 0.015 * (usr[2] - usr[1]), 
     tick_positions, tick_labels, adj = 0, cex = 0.7)

# Add legend title
text(legend_x + legend_width/2, legend_y_top + 0.05 * (usr[4] - usr[3]), 
     "KDE\n(log scale)", adj = c(0.5, 0), cex = 0.8)

par(xpd = FALSE)  # Reset to not plot outside the plot region
```

```{r}
# trying to count number of accidents near water resources individually
num_near_waterbodies <- sum(rowSums(accidents_near_waterbodies) > 0)
num_near_flowlines <- sum(rowSums(accidents_near_flowlines) > 0)

# Then, for total near water, I am combining the logical matrices 
# First, checking if they allhave same dimensions 
if (identical(dim(accidents_near_waterbodies), dim(accidents_near_flowlines))) {
  # then created a new logical matrix
  near_any_water <- matrix(FALSE, nrow=nrow(accidents_near_waterbodies), 
                          ncol=ncol(accidents_near_waterbodies))
  
  # and I set it as  TRUE if either original matrix has TRUE
  for (i in 1:nrow(accidents_near_waterbodies)) {
    for (j in 1:ncol(accidents_near_waterbodies)) {
      near_any_water[i,j] <- accidents_near_waterbodies[i,j] | accidents_near_flowlines[i,j]
    }
  }
  
  total_near_water <- sum(rowSums(near_any_water) > 0)
} else {
  # I have put an backup approach if dimensions don't match in case to avoid mismatch
  accidents_near_water_list <- lapply(1:nrow(ohio_accidents_sf), function(i) {
    any(accidents_near_waterbodies[i,]) | any(accidents_near_flowlines[i,])
  })
  total_near_water <- sum(unlist(accidents_near_water_list))
}

# Producing  a summary table 
water_summary <- data.frame(
  Category = c("Near Waterbodies (lakes, ponds)", 
               "Near Flowlines (rivers, streams)", 
               "Near Any Water Feature",
               "Total Accidents"),
  Count = c(num_near_waterbodies, 
            num_near_flowlines, 
            total_near_water,
            nrow(ohio_accidents_sf)),
  Percentage = c(num_near_waterbodies/nrow(ohio_accidents_sf)*100,
                num_near_flowlines/nrow(ohio_accidents_sf)*100,
                total_near_water/nrow(ohio_accidents_sf)*100,
                100)
)

lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

# Add Ohio fill
```

```{r}
# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

# Spatial Autocorrelation Analysis
# First I create a grid for analysis
ohio_grid <- st_make_grid(ohio_boundary, cellsize = 5000, square = TRUE) %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  mutate(grid_id = row_number())

# then I count accidents in each grid cell
grid_counts <- st_intersects(ohio_grid, ohio_accidents_sf)
ohio_grid$accident_count <- lengths(grid_counts)

# to create neighbors list using queen contiguity method
grid_nb <- poly2nb(ohio_grid, queen = TRUE)
grid_weights <- nb2listw(grid_nb, style = "W")

# and I also calculate global Moran's I
moran_i <- moran.test(ohio_grid$accident_count, grid_weights)
print(moran_i)

# Also Local Moran's I for cluster detection
local_moran <- localmoran(ohio_grid$accident_count, grid_weights)
ohio_grid$local_moran_i <- local_moran[, 1]
ohio_grid$p_value <- local_moran[, 5]

# here I am trying to identify significant clusters to check how similar each grid cell’s accident count is to its neighbors.
ohio_grid$cluster_type <- case_when(
  ohio_grid$local_moran_i > 0 & ohio_grid$accident_count > mean(ohio_grid$accident_count) & 
    ohio_grid$p_value <= 0.05 ~ "High-High",
  ohio_grid$local_moran_i > 0 & ohio_grid$accident_count < mean(ohio_grid$accident_count) & 
    ohio_grid$p_value <= 0.05 ~ "Low-Low",
  ohio_grid$local_moran_i < 0 & ohio_grid$accident_count > mean(ohio_grid$accident_count) & 
    ohio_grid$p_value <= 0.05 ~ "High-Low",
  ohio_grid$local_moran_i < 0 & ohio_grid$accident_count < mean(ohio_grid$accident_count) & 
    ohio_grid$p_value <= 0.05 ~ "Low-High",
  TRUE ~ "Not Significant"
)

# LISA cluster map
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = ohio_grid, aes(fill = cluster_type)) +
  geom_sf(data = ohio_boundary, fill = NA, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("High-High" = "red", 
                              "Low-Low" = "blue", 
                              "High-Low" = "pink", 
                              "Low-High" = "lightblue", 
                              "Not Significant" = "white")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA)",
       subtitle = "Pipeline Accidents in Ohio",
       fill = "Cluster Type")


nlcd <- rast(nlcd_path)

# Repojecting the NLCD to match prev. CRS
nlcd_proj <- project(nlcd, "EPSG:26917")

# NLCD Classes and descriptions
nlcd_classes <- data.frame(
  value = c(11, 12, 21, 22, 23, 24, 31, 41, 42, 43, 51, 52, 71, 72, 73, 74, 81, 82, 90, 95),
  class = c("Open Water", "Perennial Ice/Snow", "Developed, Open Space", "Developed, Low Intensity", 
           "Developed, Medium Intensity", "Developed, High Intensity", "Barren Land", 
           "Deciduous Forest", "Evergreen Forest", "Mixed Forest", "Dwarf Scrub", "Shrub/Scrub", 
           "Grassland/Herbaceous", "Sedge/Herbaceous", "Lichens", "Moss",

)

# Here I am extracting land use values at different accident points
# Convert accidents to terra vector for extraction
# First, converting the accidents to a SpatVector for terra
ohio_accidents_vect <- vect(ohio_accidents_sf)

# Then I  am extracting the land use classes at accident locations

colnames(landuse_freq_df) <- c("Class", "Count")
```

```{r}
    if(sum(valid_years, na.rm=TRUE) > 0) {
      # Here I only filter data of Ohio
```

```{r}
# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

# Next analysis is to Calculate directional distribution(Standard Deviational Ellipse)
# First Calculate mean center 
mean_center <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(ohio_accidents_sf)))

# then I extract the coordinates of all accident points
coords <- st_coordinates(ohio_accidents_sf)

# and calculate distance of each point from mean center
dists <- sqrt((coords[,1] - mean_center[1])^2 + (coords[,2] - mean_center[2])^2)
std_dist <- sd(dists)

# then I create a buffer like circle  with radius equal to standard distance
std_circle <- st_buffer(st_point(mean_center), std_dist) %>% st_sfc(crs = 26917)

# Then I calculate directional trend using covariance of coordinates
cov_matrix <- cov(coords)
eigen_result <- eigen(cov_matrix)
eigen_vectors <- eigen_result$vectors
eigen_values <- eigen_result$values


angle <- atan2(eigen_vectors[2,1], eigen_vectors[1,1])

# and I calculate major and minor axes
major_axis <- sqrt(eigen_values[1]) * 2  
minor_axis <- sqrt(eigen_values[2]) * 2  

# Plot 
# Transform data to geographic CRS (WGS84) for lat/long display
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)
std_circle_geo <- st_transform(std_circle, 4326)

# Transform mean center and calculate axes in geographic coordinates
mean_center_geo <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(ohio_accidents_geo)))

# Transform the axes calculations to geographic space
# Get the original angle and distances
coords_geo <- st_coordinates(ohio_accidents_geo)
cov_matrix_geo <- cov(coords_geo)
eigen_result_geo <- eigen(cov_matrix_geo)
eigen_vectors_geo <- eigen_result_geo$vectors
eigen_values_geo <- eigen_result_geo$values
angle_geo <- atan2(eigen_vectors_geo[2,1], eigen_vectors_geo[1,1])

# Calculate major and minor axes in geographic coordinates
major_axis_geo <- sqrt(eigen_values_geo[1]) * 2
minor_axis_geo <- sqrt(eigen_values_geo[2]) * 2

# Set up the plotting area
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA, 
     border = NA,
     axes = FALSE,
     main = "Directional Distribution of Pipeline Accidents in Ohio")

# Get the bounding box for grid lines
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)

# Create latitude and longitude breaks
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 2), "° W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}
for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Add Ohio fill
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = "white",
     border = NA,
     add = TRUE)

# Plot the standard distance circle
plot(st_geometry(std_circle_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "blue",
     lwd = 1,
     add = TRUE)

# Add the major axis arrow
arrows(
  mean_center_geo[1], mean_center_geo[2],
  mean_center_geo[1] + cos(angle_geo) * major_axis_geo,
  mean_center_geo[2] + sin(angle_geo) * major_axis_geo,
  col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, length = 0.10
)

# Add the minor axis arrow
arrows(
  mean_center_geo[1], mean_center_geo[2],
  mean_center_geo[1] + cos(angle_geo + pi/2) * minor_axis_geo,
  mean_center_geo[2] + sin(angle_geo + pi/2) * minor_axis_geo,
  col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, length = 0.10
)

# Add Ohio boundary
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "black",
     lwd = 0.5,
     add = TRUE)

# Plot the accident points
plot(st_geometry(ohio_accidents_geo),
     col = "red",
     pch = 16,
     cex = 1.5,
     add = TRUE)

# Add subtitle
mtext("Mean Center, Standard Distance, and Principal Axes",
      side = 3, line = -0.1, cex = 0.8)

# Add manual axes with lat/long labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# Add scale bar
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the plot area
box()

# Add a custom legend
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c("Accident Locations", "Standard Distance", "Major Axis", "Minor Axis"),
       col = c("red", "blue", "darkblue", "darkgreen"),
       pch = c(16, NA, NA, NA),
       lty = c(NA, 1, 1, 1),
       lwd = c(NA, 1, 2, 2),
       pt.cex = 1.5,
       bty = "n",
       cex = 0.8,
       title = "Map Elements")
```

```{r}
# 3. Directional Distribution Statistics

  Value = c(

    round(mean_center[2], 2),

  )
)

# 4. LISA Cluster statistics
if(exists("ohio_grid") && "cluster_type" %in% names(ohio_grid)) {
  # Count by cluster type

  cluster_type_stats <- data.frame(
    Cluster_Type = names(cluster_counts),
    Count = as.numeric(cluster_counts),

  )
  print("LISA Cluster Type Statistics:")
  print(cluster_type_stats)
  
  # here I count number of accidents in each cluster type
  accidents_in_clusters <- list()
  for(cluster_type in unique(ohio_grid$cluster_type)) {
    grid_cells <- ohio_grid[ohio_grid$cluster_type == cluster_type, ]
    accidents_in_cells <- st_intersects(grid_cells, ohio_accidents_sf)
    accidents_in_clusters[[cluster_type]] <- sum(lengths(accidents_in_cells))
  }
  accidents_by_cluster <- data.frame(
    Cluster_Type = names(accidents_in_clusters),
    Accident_Count = unlist(accidents_in_clusters),
    Percentage = round(unlist(accidents_in_clusters) / nrow(ohio_accidents_sf) * 100, 2)
  )
  print("Accidents by Cluster Type:")
  print(accidents_by_cluster)
}

# 5. then also bring in Land use statistics for accidents
if(exists("landuse_freq_df")) {
  print("Land Use Distribution of Accidents:")
  print(landuse_freq_df)
}

# and I produce a comprehensive summary dataframe for the report

  ),

                 " with ", max(annual_counts$Accidents), " accidents"),

                 ", p < ", format.pval(moran_i$p.value, digits = 2), ")"),

    paste0("Accidents show a directional trend (", round(angle * 180/pi, 1), 
          "° orientation) with elongation ratio of ", round(major_axis/minor_axis, 2)),
    
    ifelse(exists("landuse_freq_df"),

  )
)

print("Segment 2 Summary for Report:")
```

```{r}
# Hotspot Detection using Kernel Density Estimation(KDE)

# I am creating a point pattern object for KDE
library(spatstat)
ohio_win <- as.owin(st_geometry(ohio_boundary))
ohio_pts <- st_coordinates(ohio_accidents_sf)
ohio_ppp <- ppp(ohio_pts[,1], ohio_pts[,2], window = ohio_win)

bw_cv <- bw.diggle(ohio_ppp)
print(paste("Optimal bandwidth from cross-validation:", round(bw_cv, 2), "meters"))

# I am implementing Silverman's rule of thumb incase computation is intense to avoid session crashout
n <- npoints(ohio_ppp)
sigma_x <- sd(ohio_pts[,1])
sigma_y <- sd(ohio_pts[,2])
sigma <- (sigma_x + sigma_y) / 2
bw_silverman <- 0.9 * sigma * n^(-0.2)
print(paste("Silverman's rule of thumb bandwidth:", round(bw_silverman, 2), "meters"))

# Then i select a suitable bandwidth 
bandwidth <- 10000  

# and I compute the KDE
ohio_density <- density.ppp(ohio_ppp, sigma = bandwidth)

# then I convert KDE to a raster for easier analysis
library(terra)
density_rast <- rast(ohio_density)
crs(density_rast) <- "EPSG:26917" 

# and I calculate statistics for the density values
density_values <- values(density_rast)
density_stats <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Minimum Density", "Maximum Density", "Mean Density", "Median Density"),
  Value = c(min(density_values, na.rm = TRUE), 
           max(density_values, na.rm = TRUE),
           mean(density_values, na.rm = TRUE),
           median(density_values, na.rm = TRUE))
)
print("Kernel Density Statistics:")
print(density_stats)

# here I identify hotspots using a threshold approach

density_mean <- mean(density_values, na.rm = TRUE)
density_sd <- sd(density_values, na.rm = TRUE)
hotspot_threshold <- density_mean + 2 * density_sd

# I am creating a hotspot mask
hotspot_mask <- density_rast > hotspot_threshold
names(hotspot_mask) <- "hotspot"

# so I can calculate area of hotspots
hotspot_cells <- sum(values(hotspot_mask), na.rm = TRUE)
cell_area <- prod(res(hotspot_mask)) / 1000000  # cell area in sq km
hotspot_area <- hotspot_cells * cell_area
total_area <- ncell(hotspot_mask) * cell_area
hotspot_percentage <- (hotspot_area / total_area) * 100

# then I convert hotspot mask to vector for intersection with point data
hotspot_polygons <- as.polygons(hotspot_mask, dissolve = TRUE)
hotspot_sf <- st_as_sf(hotspot_polygons)

# trying to count accidents in hotspots
accidents_in_hotspots <- st_intersects(ohio_accidents_sf, hotspot_sf)
num_in_hotspots <- sum(lengths(accidents_in_hotspots) > 0)
pct_in_hotspots <- (num_in_hotspots / nrow(ohio_accidents_sf)) * 100

# also I am calculating hotspot intensity accidents per sq km within hotspots
hotspot_intensity <- num_in_hotspots / hotspot_area

# Summarizing all the hotspot stats
hotspot_stats <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c(
    "Hotspot Threshold Value", 
    "Number of Hotspots", 
    "Total Hotspot Area (sq km)", 
    "Percentage of Ohio in Hotspots", 
    "Number of Accidents in Hotspots", 
    "Percentage of Accidents in Hotspots",
    "Accident Density in Hotspots (per sq km)"
  ),
  Value = c(
    round(hotspot_threshold, 8),
    length(unique(st_cast(hotspot_sf, "POLYGON"))),
    round(hotspot_area, 2),
    round(hotspot_percentage, 2),
    num_in_hotspots,
    round(pct_in_hotspots, 2),
    round(hotspot_intensity, 2)
  )
)
print("Hotspot Analysis Statistics:")
print(hotspot_stats)

# here I am trying to analyze land use within hotspots
if(exists("nlcd_proj")) {
  # so I first extract land use values from hotspot areas
  hotspot_landuse <- terra::extract(nlcd_proj, hotspot_polygons)
  
  # then I calculate land use frequencies
  hotspot_landuse_freq <- table(hotspot_landuse$Class)
  hotspot_landuse_freq_df <- as.data.frame(hotspot_landuse_freq)
  names(hotspot_landuse_freq_df) <- c("Class", "Count")
  hotspot_landuse_freq_df$Percentage <- hotspot_landuse_freq_df$Count / sum(hotspot_landuse_freq_df$Count) * 100
  
  # and I sort it order by count
  hotspot_landuse_freq_df <- hotspot_landuse_freq_df[order(-hotspot_landuse_freq_df$Count),]
  
  print("Land Use Distribution within Hotspots:")
  print(head(hotspot_landuse_freq_df, 10))
}

# Map
ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = st_as_stars(density_rast)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Density", option = "plasma") +
  geom_sf(data = hotspot_sf, fill = NA, color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = ohio_boundary, fill = NA, color = "black") +
  geom_sf(data = ohio_accidents_sf, size = 1, color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Kernel Density Estimation and Hotspots of Pipeline Accidents in Ohio",
       subtitle = paste0("Hotspots defined as areas with density > 2 standard deviations above mean\n",
                        num_in_hotspots, " of ", nrow(ohio_accidents_sf), 
                        " accidents (", round(pct_in_hotspots, 1), "%) occur in hotspots")) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")


# I also calculating the distance from accidents to the nearest hotspot centroid
hotspot_centroids <- st_centroid(st_cast(hotspot_sf, "POLYGON"))
distances_to_hotspots <- st_distance(ohio_accidents_sf, hotspot_centroids)
min_distances <- apply(distances_to_hotspots, 1, min)

# I create a dataframe for Distance related stats
distance_stats <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Minimum Distance to Hotspot", "Mean Distance to Hotspot", 
               "Median Distance to Hotspot", "Maximum Distance to Hotspot"),
  Value = c(min(min_distances), mean(min_distances), 
           median(min_distances), max(min_distances))
)
distance_stats$Value <- round(as.numeric(distance_stats$Value))
print("Distance to Hotspot Statistics (meters):")
print(distance_stats)

# printing summary
hotspot_summary <- data.frame(
  Analysis_Component = "Hotspot Detection (KDE)",
  Key_Finding = paste0(
    round(pct_in_hotspots, 1), "% of accidents occur in hotspots covering only ", 
    round(hotspot_percentage, 1), "% of Ohio's area, with an accident density of ",
    round(hotspot_intensity, 1), " accidents per sq km"
  )
)

print("Hotspot Analysis Summary for Report:")
print(hotspot_summary)
```

```{r}
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 2), "° W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}
for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Plot the population density choropleth
plot(st_geometry(ohio_tracts_geo),
     col = viridis_colors[findInterval(ohio_tracts_geo$pop_density, pop_breaks)],
     border = NA,
     add = TRUE)

# Add tract boundaries (very light)
plot(st_geometry(ohio_tracts_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "#FFFFFF20",  # Very light white with transparency
     lwd = 0.1,
     add = TRUE)

# Plot the accident points
plot(st_geometry(ohio_accidents_geo),
     col = "red",
     pch = 16,
     cex = 0.8,
     add = TRUE)

# Add subtitle
mtext("Population density (people per sq km) with accident locations",
      side = 3, line = -0.1, cex = 0.8)

# Add manual axes with lat/long labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# Add scale bar
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the plot area
box()

# Create a custom legend for population density
legend_title <- "Population\nDensity"
legend_labels <- c("10", "100", "1,000", "10,000")
legend("right", 
       legend = legend_labels,
       fill = viridis_colors,
       border = "#FFFFFF20",
       bty = "n",
       cex = 0.8,
       title = legend_title)
```

```{r}
# I conduct a Buffer Analysis around accident points 
# so I first create multiple buffers around accident points (500m, 1km, 3km)
buffer_500m <- st_buffer(ohio_accidents_sf, 500)
buffer_1km <- st_buffer(ohio_accidents_sf, 1000)
buffer_3km <- st_buffer(ohio_accidents_sf, 3000)

# then I dissolve buffers to avoid double-counting population
buffer_500m_dissolved <- st_union(buffer_500m)
buffer_1km_dissolved <- st_union(buffer_1km)
buffer_3km_dissolved <- st_union(buffer_3km)

# and I convert them all to sf objects
buffer_500m_sf <- st_sf(geometry = buffer_500m_dissolved)
buffer_1km_sf <- st_sf(geometry = buffer_1km_dissolved)
buffer_3km_sf <- st_sf(geometry = buffer_3km_dissolved)

# and I calculate area of each buffer zone
buffer_500m_sf$area_sqkm <- as.numeric(st_area(buffer_500m_sf) / 1000000)
buffer_1km_sf$area_sqkm <- as.numeric(st_area(buffer_1km_sf) / 1000000)
buffer_3km_sf$area_sqkm <- as.numeric(st_area(buffer_3km_sf) / 1000000)

# and then to calculate the population within each buffer zone
# I use an area-weighted approach for tracts that are partially within buffers
population_500m <- st_interpolate_aw(
  ohio_tracts_sf["estimate"], 
  buffer_500m_sf, 
  extensive = TRUE
)

population_1km <- st_interpolate_aw(
  ohio_tracts_sf["estimate"], 
  buffer_1km_sf, 
  extensive = TRUE
)

population_3km <- st_interpolate_aw(
  ohio_tracts_sf["estimate"], 
  buffer_3km_sf, 
  extensive = TRUE
)

# so I extract the population values
pop_500m <- sum(population_500m$estimate)
pop_1km <- sum(population_1km$estimate)
pop_3km <- sum(population_3km$estimate)

# and get total Ohio population for comparison
total_ohio_pop <- sum(ohio_tracts_sf$estimate)

# and then I calculate population density in each buffer zone
pop_density_500m <- pop_500m / buffer_500m_sf$area_sqkm
pop_density_1km <- pop_1km / buffer_1km_sf$area_sqkm
pop_density_3km <- pop_3km / buffer_3km_sf$area_sqkm

# Summary table for report 
population_exposure <- data.frame(
  Buffer_Distance = c("500m", "1km", "3km", "All of Ohio"),
  Area_SqKm = c(buffer_500m_sf$area_sqkm, buffer_1km_sf$area_sqkm, buffer_3km_sf$area_sqkm, sum(as.numeric(ohio_tracts_sf$area_sqkm))),
  Population = c(pop_500m, pop_1km, pop_3km, total_ohio_pop),
  Population_Density = c(pop_density_500m, pop_density_1km, pop_density_3km, total_ohio_pop / sum(as.numeric(ohio_tracts_sf$area_sqkm))),
  Percentage_of_Ohio_Pop = c(pop_500m / total_ohio_pop * 100, pop_1km / total_ohio_pop * 100, pop_3km / total_ohio_pop * 100, 100)
)

# View results
print(population_exposure)
```

```{r}
print(head(ohio_socioeconomic_pop))
str(ohio_socioeconomic_pop)

# loading the tract file
geometry_path <- "~/Assignment/cb_2019_39_tract_500k/cb_2019_39_tract_500k.shp"
ohio_tracts_boundaries <- st_read(geometry_path)


# checking the geometry 
print(head(ohio_tracts_boundaries))
str(ohio_tracts_boundaries)

# Then I do the Join between the two 
# because both datasets  share a common identifier ('GEOID')
ohio_socioeconomic <- left_join(ohio_tracts_boundaries, ohio_socioeconomic_pop, by = "GEOID")


ohio_socioeconomic <- left_join(ohio_tracts_boundaries, ohio_socioeconomic_pop, by = "GEOID")

# then i convert it to a non-spatial dataframe for reshaping later
ohio_geo <- ohio_socioeconomic %>%
  dplyr::select(GEOID, geometry)

ohio_socioeconomic_df <- ohio_socioeconomic %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%       # explicitly sf’s drop
  dplyr::select(-moe)

print(names(ohio_socioeconomic_df))



if ("NAME.y" %in% names(ohio_socioeconomic_df)) {
  ohio_socioeconomic_df <- ohio_socioeconomic_df %>% rename(NAME = NAME.y)
} else if (!"NAME" %in% names(ohio_socioeconomic_df)) {
  
  ohio_socioconomic_df <- ohio_socioeconomic_df %>%
    mutate(NAME = ifelse(!is.na(NAME.x) & NAME.x != "", NAME.x, GEOID))
}


ohio_socioeconomic_df <- ohio_socioeconomic_df %>% select(-NAME.x)

# here I reshape the the dataset
ohio_socioeconomic_wide <- ohio_socioeconomic_df %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(GEOID, NAME),  # now 'NAME' holds the descriptive information
    names_from = variable,
    values_from = estimate
  )

# then I do the join with geometry and convert it into an sf Object
ohio_socioeconomic_wide <- ohio_socioeconomic_wide %>%
  left_join(ohio_geo, by = "GEOID") %>%
  st_sf()

# Checking if join has been successful or not
print(names(ohio_socioeconomic_wide))

# i am checking if there any NA values in socioeconmic variables
na_count <- colSums(is.na(st_drop_geometry(ohio_socioeconomic_wide)))
print("NA counts in socioeconomic variables:")
print(na_count)

# then I calculate the vulnerability metrics
ohio_socioeconomic_wide <- ohio_socioeconomic_wide %>%
  mutate(
    # I calculate poverty rate (%)
    poverty_rate = ifelse(population > 0, poverty / population * 100, NA),
    # then also calculate low education rate (%), using edu_total as denominator
    low_edu_rate = ifelse(edu_total > 0, no_hs / edu_total * 100, NA)
  )

# Summarize the calculated rates for checking
rate_summary <- ohio_socioeconomic_wide %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% summarise(
  poverty_rate_min = min(poverty_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
  poverty_rate_max = max(poverty_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
  poverty_rate_mean = mean(poverty_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
  low_edu_rate_min = min(low_edu_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
  low_edu_rate_max = max(low_edu_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
  low_edu_rate_mean = mean(low_edu_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
)
print("Summary of calculated rates:")
print(rate_summary)

# I have decided to Normalize Socioeconomic Metrics 
ohio_socioeconomic_wide <- ohio_socioeconomic_wide %>%
  mutate(
    # because For income, higher values are less vulnerable, so I am inverting the normalization
    income_range = max(income, na.rm = TRUE) - min(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    income_norm = ifelse(income_range > 0, (max(income, na.rm = TRUE) - income) / income_range, 0),
    
    # and For poverty, higher rates mean more vulnerability
    poverty_range = max(poverty_rate, na.rm = TRUE) - min(poverty_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    poverty_norm = ifelse(poverty_range > 0, (poverty_rate - min(poverty_rate, na.rm = TRUE)) / poverty_range, 0),
    
    # likewise for low education, higher rates mean more vulnerability
    edu_range = max(low_edu_rate, na.rm = TRUE) - min(low_edu_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    edu_norm = ifelse(edu_range > 0, (low_edu_rate - min(low_edu_rate, na.rm = TRUE)) / edu_range, 0)
  )

# Computing a vulnerability index with a NA handling capacity 
ohio_socioeconomic_wide <- ohio_socioeconomic_wide %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    valid_indicators = sum(!is.na(c(income_norm, poverty_norm, edu_norm))),
    vulnerability_index = ifelse(valid_indicators > 0,
                                 sum(c(income_norm, poverty_norm, edu_norm), na.rm = TRUE) / valid_indicators,
                                 NA)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

vuln_summary <- summary(ohio_socioeconomic_wide$vulnerability_index)
print("Vulnerability index summary:")
print(vuln_summary)

# ensuring consistent CRS across the sf buffer
buffer_3km_sf <- st_transform(buffer_3km_sf, st_crs(ohio_socioeconomic_wide))



# Here I am trying to analyse the vulnerability within the buffer zones 
tracts_in_buffer <- st_intersects(ohio_socioeconomic_wide, buffer_3km_sf)
ohio_socioeconomic_wide$in_buffer <- lengths(tracts_in_buffer) > 0


vuln_in_buffer <- mean(ohio_socioeconomic_wide$vulnerability_index[ohio_socioeconomic_wide$in_buffer], na.rm = TRUE)
vuln_all_ohio <- mean(ohio_socioeconomic_wide$vulnerability_index, na.rm = TRUE)

vulnerability_comparison <- data.frame(
  Region = c("3km Buffer Zone Around Accidents", "Ohio Overall"),
  Average_Vulnerability_Index = c(vuln_in_buffer, vuln_all_ohio),
  Relative_Vulnerability = c(vuln_in_buffer / vuln_all_ohio * 100, 100)
)
print("Vulnerability comparison:")
print(vulnerability_comparison)

# I am calculating Population in Vulnerable Areas

quantile_75 <- quantile(ohio_socioeconomic_wide$vulnerability_index, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
ohio_socioeconomic_wide$high_vulnerability <- ohio_socioeconomic_wide$vulnerability_index >= quantile_75

# Trying to obtain Population in high-vulnerability tracts within the 3km buffer
high_vuln_pop_in_buffer <- sum(ohio_socioeconomic_wide$population[ohio_socioeconomic_wide$in_buffer & ohio_socioeconomic_wide$high_vulnerability], na.rm = TRUE)
total_pop_in_buffer <- sum(ohio_socioeconomic_wide$population[ohio_socioeconomic_wide$in_buffer], na.rm = TRUE)
high_vuln_pct_in_buffer <- high_vuln_pop_in_buffer / total_pop_in_buffer * 100

# and then getting the overall high vulnerability population percentage
high_vuln_pop_overall <- sum(ohio_socioeconomic_wide$population[ohio_socioeconomic_wide$high_vulnerability], na.rm = TRUE)
total_pop_overall <- sum(ohio_socioeconomic_wide$population, na.rm = TRUE)
high_vuln_pct_overall <- high_vuln_pop_overall / total_pop_overall * 100

vulnerable_pop_stats <- data.frame(
  Region = c("3km Buffer Zone", "Ohio Overall"),
  Total_Population = c(total_pop_in_buffer, total_pop_overall),
  High_Vulnerability_Population = c(high_vuln_pop_in_buffer, high_vuln_pop_overall),
  Percentage_High_Vulnerability = c(high_vuln_pct_in_buffer, high_vuln_pct_overall)
)
```

```{r}
nlcd_proj <- project(nlcd, "EPSG:26917")

# Then I extract NLCD classes at accident locations
ohio_accidents_vect <- vect(ohio_accidents_sf)
accident_nlcd <- terra::extract(nlcd_proj, ohio_accidents_vect)

# and I check what we have from extraction
head(accident_nlcd)

# and I get frequency table of land use at accident locations
accident_landuse_freq <- table(accident_nlcd$Class)
print("NLCD class distribution at accident locations:")
print(accident_landuse_freq)

developed_mask <- ifel(nlcd_proj %in% c("Developed, Open Space", 
                                        "Developed, Low Intensity", 
                                        "Developed, Medium Intensity", 
                                        "Developed High Intensity"), 1, NA)

# here I convert the developed mask to polygons
developed_areas <- as.polygons(developed_mask, dissolve=TRUE)
developed_areas_sf <- st_as_sf(developed_areas)

# then I calculate distance from each accident to the nearest developed area
if(nrow(developed_areas_sf) > 0) {
  # and I transform it to right CRS
  developed_areas_sf <- st_transform(developed_areas_sf, st_crs(ohio_accidents_sf))
  
  # then I calculate distances
  distances_to_urban <- st_distance(ohio_accidents_sf, developed_areas_sf)
  
  # and I get minimum distance for each accident
  min_dist_to_urban <- apply(distances_to_urban, 1, min)
  
  # I push all the accidents data to dataframe
  ohio_accidents_sf$dist_to_urban <- min_dist_to_urban
  
  # and I classify accidents by proximity to urban areas
  ohio_accidents_sf$urban_proximity <- cut(
    as.numeric(ohio_accidents_sf$dist_to_urban),
    breaks = c(0, 100, 1000, 5000, Inf),
    labels = c("In Urban", "Adjacent to Urban (<100m)", "Near Urban (100m-1km)", "Rural (>1km)"),
    include.lowest = TRUE
  )
  
  # and I calculate summary stats
  urban_proximity_stats <- table(ohio_accidents_sf$urban_proximity)
  urban_proximity_pct <- prop.table(urban_proximity_stats) * 100
  
  # and I create a summary dataframe
  urban_proximity_summary <- data.frame(
    Proximity_Category = names(urban_proximity_stats),
    Accident_Count = as.numeric(urban_proximity_stats),
    Percentage = as.numeric(urban_proximity_pct)
  )
  
  # Print urban proximity stats
  print("Pipeline Accidents by Proximity to Urban Areas (NLCD-based):")
  print(urban_proximity_summary)
}
```

```{r}
# I count accidents in each grid cell
accident_counts <- st_intersects(risk_grid_simple, ohio_accidents_sf)
risk_grid_simple$accident_count <- lengths(accident_counts)
risk_grid_simple$area_sq_km <- as.numeric(st_area(risk_grid_simple) / 1000000)
risk_grid_simple$accident_density <- risk_grid_simple$accident_count / risk_grid_simple$area_sq_km

# I am printing summary of accident counts per grid cell to check 
print(summary(risk_grid_simple$accident_count))

# then I add population data to each grid cell
# and I use simpler interpolation that won't cause dimension mismatches
risk_grid_simple$population <- 0

# here I directly calculate population in each grid cell using point-in-polygon operation
# First I convert population data to points at centroids
ohio_tracts_points <- st_centroid(ohio_tracts_sf)
ohio_tracts_points$population <- ohio_tracts_sf$estimate

# and I assign population to grid cells
for(i in 1:nrow(risk_grid_simple)) {
  # and I find tract centroids within this grid cell
  tracts_in_cell <- st_intersects(risk_grid_simple[i,], ohio_tracts_points)
  if(length(tracts_in_cell[[1]]) > 0) {
    # and I sum population from all tract centroids in this cell
    risk_grid_simple$population[i] <- sum(ohio_tracts_points$population[tracts_in_cell[[1]]])
  }
}

# so I can obtain and calculate population density
risk_grid_simple$pop_density <- risk_grid_simple$population / risk_grid_simple$area_sq_km
print(summary(risk_grid_simple$population))

water_cells <- st_intersects(risk_grid_simple, nhd_waterbodies_proj)
flowline_cells <- st_intersects(risk_grid_simple, nhd_flowline_proj_clean)

# then I mark cells that contain water features
risk_grid_simple$has_waterbody <- lengths(water_cells) > 0
risk_grid_simple$has_flowline <- lengths(flowline_cells) > 0
risk_grid_simple$has_water <- risk_grid_simple$has_waterbody | risk_grid_simple$has_flowline
risk_grid_simple$water_factor <- as.numeric(risk_grid_simple$has_water)

# and I print water feature presence
water_presence <- table(risk_grid_simple$has_water)
print("Grid cells containing water features:")
print(water_presence)


# I do the normalizzation process for having risk factors ( from 0 to 1 scale )

max_acc_density <- max(risk_grid_simple$accident_density, na.rm = TRUE)
risk_grid_simple$accident_norm <- risk_grid_simple$accident_density / max_acc_density

max_pop_density <- max(risk_grid_simple$pop_density, na.rm = TRUE)
risk_grid_simple$pop_norm <- risk_grid_simple$pop_density / max_pop_density

# Then I calculate integrated risk index
risk_grid_simple$risk_index <- (0.5 * risk_grid_simple$accident_norm) + 
                              (0.3 * risk_grid_simple$pop_norm) + 
                              (0.2 * risk_grid_simple$water_factor)

# Finally here I categorize risk levels
risk_breaks <- quantile(risk_grid_simple$risk_index, 
                       probs = c(0, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.975, 1), 
                       na.rm = TRUE)
risk_grid_simple$risk_category <- cut(risk_grid_simple$risk_index, 
                                    breaks = risk_breaks,
                                    labels = c("Very Low", "Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"),
                                    include.lowest = TRUE)

# so I can generate risk stats
risk_stats <- data.frame(
  Risk_Category = levels(risk_grid_simple$risk_category),
  Cell_Count = as.numeric(table(risk_grid_simple$risk_category)),
  Area_Sq_Km = tapply(risk_grid_simple$area_sq_km, risk_grid_simple$risk_category, sum),
  Area_Percent = tapply(risk_grid_simple$area_sq_km, risk_grid_simple$risk_category, sum) / 
                sum(risk_grid_simple$area_sq_km) * 100,
  Population = tapply(risk_grid_simple$population, risk_grid_simple$risk_category, sum),
  Population_Percent = tapply(risk_grid_simple$population, risk_grid_simple$risk_category, sum) / 
                      sum(risk_grid_simple$population) * 100,
  Accident_Count = tapply(risk_grid_simple$accident_count, risk_grid_simple$risk_category, sum),
  Accident_Percent = tapply(risk_grid_simple$accident_count, risk_grid_simple$risk_category, sum) / 
                    sum(risk_grid_simple$accident_count) * 100
)

# and print risk stats
print("Integrated Risk Assessment Statistics:")
print(risk_stats)

#— Load libraries
library(sf)
library(mapsf)
library(viridisLite)

#— 1. Reproject all layers to geographic CRS (WGS84) for neat axes
risk_grid_geo      <- st_transform(risk_grid_simple, 4326)
ohio_boundary_geo  <- st_transform(ohio_boundary,     4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)

#— 2. Ensure risk_category is a factor with desired order
risk_grid_geo$risk_category <- factor(
  risk_grid_geo$risk_category,
  levels = c("Very Low","Low","Moderate","High","Very High")
)

#— 3. Create a reversed Inferno palette matching the levels
pal_vals <- viridisLite::inferno(length(levels(risk_grid_geo$risk_category)), direction = -1)
names(pal_vals) <- levels(risk_grid_geo$risk_category)

#— 4. Set tight margins (bottom, left, top, right)
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))

#— 5. Empty base plot with title + subtitle
plot(
  st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
  col      = NA,
  border   = NA,
  axes     = FALSE,
  main     = paste0(
               "Integrated Risk Assessment for Pipeline Accidents in Ohio\n",
               "Combining accident density, population exposure, and environmental factors"
             ),
  cex.main = 0.7
)

#— 6. Gridlines & lat/long labels
bbox       <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)
lon_labels <- paste0(abs(round(lon_breaks, 2)), "°", ifelse(lon_breaks < 0, "W", "E"))
lat_labels <- paste0(abs(round(lat_breaks, 2)), "°", ifelse(lat_breaks < 0, "S", "N"))

for (x in lon_breaks) abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
for (y in lat_breaks) abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)

#— 7. Choropleth of risk categories (no built-in legend)
mf_map(
  x        = risk_grid_geo,
  type     = "typo",
  var      = "risk_category",
  pal      = pal_vals,
  border   = NA,
  add      = TRUE,
  leg_pos  = NA    # suppress the default legend
)

#— 8. Custom legend showing only the five risk levels
mf_legend(
  type  = "typo",
  pos   = "right",
  val   = levels(risk_grid_geo$risk_category),
  pal   = pal_vals,
  title = "Risk Level"
)

#— 9. Overlay state boundary for crisp edge
mf_map(
  x      = ohio_boundary_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = NA,
  border = "black",
  lwd    = 0.5,
  add    = TRUE
)

#— 10. Accident points
mf_map(
  x      = ohio_accidents_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = "black",
  pch    = 19,
  cex    = 0.5,
  add    = TRUE
)

#— 11. Axes, north arrow, scale bar, and frame box
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft")
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")
box()
```

```{r}
# I am creating separate kernel density estimates for each decade
library(spatstat)

# so I start with creating a spatial window for point pattern analysis using Ohio boundary
ohio_win <- as.owin(st_geometry(ohio_boundary))

# and then I function to create KDE for a specific decade
create_kde_for_decade <- function(decade_data, window, bandwidth = 15000) {
  # then convert to spatstat ppp object
  coords <- st_coordinates(decade_data)
  if(nrow(coords) > 0) {
    ppp_obj <- ppp(coords[,1], coords[,2], window = window)
    # and then simply alculate density
    density_obj <- density.ppp(ppp_obj, sigma = bandwidth)
    return(density_obj)
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
}

# this is where I create KDEs for each decade
kde_1980s <- create_kde_for_decade(accidents_1980s, ohio_win)
kde_1990s <- create_kde_for_decade(accidents_1990s, ohio_win)
kde_2000s <- create_kde_for_decade(accidents_2000s, ohio_win)
kde_2010s <- create_kde_for_decade(accidents_2010s, ohio_win)

# and convert to rasters for visualization
library(terra)
rast_1980s <- rast(kde_1980s)
rast_1990s <- rast(kde_1990s)
rast_2000s <- rast(kde_2000s)
rast_2010s <- rast(kde_2010s)

# I am ensuring consistency in CRS
crs(rast_1980s) <- "EPSG:26917"
crs(rast_1990s) <- "EPSG:26917"
crs(rast_2000s) <- "EPSG:26917"
crs(rast_2010s) <- "EPSG:26917"

# I am calculating the maximum density value across all decades for consistent scaling
max_density <- max(
  max(values(rast_1980s), na.rm = TRUE),
  max(values(rast_1990s), na.rm = TRUE),
  max(values(rast_2000s), na.rm = TRUE),
  max(values(rast_2010s), na.rm = TRUE)
)

# so I can calculate centroids for each decade later
centroid_1980s <- st_centroid(st_union(accidents_1980s))
centroid_1990s <- st_centroid(st_union(accidents_1990s))
centroid_2000s <- st_centroid(st_union(accidents_2000s))
centroid_2010s <- st_centroid(st_union(accidents_2010s))

# and calculate distance between centroids to see if hotspots have shifted over time
centroid_shifts <- data.frame(
  Decades = c("1980s to 1990s", "1990s to 2000s", "2000s to 2010s"),
  Distance_km = c(
    as.numeric(st_distance(centroid_1980s, centroid_1990s)) / 1000,
    as.numeric(st_distance(centroid_1990s, centroid_2000s)) / 1000,
    as.numeric(st_distance(centroid_2000s, centroid_2010s)) / 1000
  )
)

print("Shift in accident hotspot centroids over time (km):")
print(centroid_shifts)
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(mapsf)
library(viridisLite)

# 1) Reproject everything to WGS84 so axes are in °N/°W
ohio_counties_geo <- st_transform(ohio_counties_sf, 4326)
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)

# 2) Compute your gridlines & labels once
bbox    <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)
lon_br  <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_br  <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)
lon_lb  <- paste0(abs(round(lon_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lon_br<0,"W","E"))
lat_lb  <- paste0(abs(round(lat_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lat_br<0,"N","N"))

# 3) Shared Plasma palette
pal100 <- viridisLite::plasma(100, direction = -1)

# 4) Helper to draw the blank base + grids + title
draw_base <- function(title) {
  par(mar = c(3,3,2,1))
  plot(
    st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
    col    = NA,
    border = NA,
    axes   = FALSE,
    main   = title,
    cex.main = 1.2
  )
  for(x in lon_br) abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lty = 2)
  for(y in lat_br) abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lty = 2)
}

# 5) Helper to overlay boundary, axes, arrow, scale & box
add_axes <- function() {
  mf_map(
    x      = ohio_boundary_geo,
    type   = "base",
    col    = NA,
    border = "black",
    add    = TRUE
  )
  axis(1, at = lon_br, labels = lon_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
  axis(2, at = lat_br, labels = lat_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
  mf_arrow(pos = "topleft")
  mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")
  box()
}

#–– Map 1: Accident counts ––
draw_base("Pipeline Accidents by County in Ohio")

# Create quantile breaks for accident count - fixed approach
count_values <- ohio_counties_geo$accident_count
# For quantiles, we'll use the stats::quantile function
count_breaks <- c(
  0,  # start at 0
  stats::quantile(
    count_values[count_values > 0],  # skip zeros for better breaks
    probs = seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.2)
  ),
  max(count_values)  # end at max value
)

# Create a custom color palette with 7 colors (for 6 intervals)
count_pal <- pal100[seq(1, 100, length.out = length(count_breaks) - 1)]

mf_map(
  x        = ohio_counties_geo,
  type     = "choro",
  var      = "accident_count",
  breaks   = count_breaks,
  pal      = count_pal,
  border   = "grey70",
  lwd      = 0.4,
  add      = TRUE,
  leg_pos  = NA
)

# Custom legend
mf_legend(
  type   = "choro",
  pos    = "right",
  title  = "Number of\nAccidents",
  val    = count_breaks,
  pal    = count_pal,
  frame  = TRUE
)
add_axes()

#–– Map 2: Accident rate per 1000 km² ––
draw_base("Pipeline Accident Rate by County in Ohio")

# Create quantile breaks for accident rate
rate_values <- ohio_counties_geo$accident_rate
rate_breaks <- c(
  0,  # start at 0
  stats::quantile(
    rate_values[rate_values > 0],  # skip zeros for better breaks
    probs = seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.2)
  ),
  max(rate_values)  # end at max value
)

# Create a custom color palette
rate_pal <- pal100[seq(1, 100, length.out = length(rate_breaks) - 1)]

mf_map(
  x        = ohio_counties_geo,
  type     = "choro",
  var      = "accident_rate",
  breaks   = rate_breaks,
  pal      = rate_pal,
  border   = "grey70",
  lwd      = 0.4,
  add      = TRUE,
  leg_pos  = NA
)

mf_legend(
  type   = "choro",
  pos    = "right",
  title  = "Accidents per\n1000 sq km",
  val    = rate_breaks,
  pal    = rate_pal,
  frame  = TRUE
)
add_axes()

#–– Map 3: Population-weighted risk per 100,000 people ––
draw_base("Population-Weighted Pipeline Accident Risk by County")

# Create quantile breaks for population risk
risk_values <- ohio_counties_geo$pop_risk
risk_breaks <- c(
  0,  # start at 0
  stats::quantile(
    risk_values[risk_values > 0],  # skip zeros for better breaks
    probs = seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.2)
  ),
  max(risk_values)  # end at max value
)

# Create a custom color palette
risk_pal <- pal100[seq(1, 100, length.out = length(risk_breaks) - 1)]

mf_map(
  x        = ohio_counties_geo,
  type     = "choro",
  var      = "pop_risk",
  breaks   = risk_breaks,
  pal      = risk_pal,
  border   = "grey70",
  lwd      = 0.4,
  add      = TRUE,
  leg_pos  = NA
)

mf_legend(
  type   = "choro",
  pos    = "right",
  title  = "Accidents per\n100,000 people",
  val    = risk_breaks,
  pal    = risk_pal,
  frame  = TRUE
)
add_axes()
```

```{r}
# I am trying to generate Thiessen/Voronoi polygons for pipeline accident service areas

# First I create the Voronoi polygons
thiessen_polygons <- ohio_accidents_sf %>%
  st_union() %>%                          
  st_voronoi() %>%                        
  st_collection_extract() %>%             
  st_intersection(ohio_boundary)     

# so I assign accident attributes to each polygon using nearest accident
# Instead of directly using st_intersects (which assumed a 1:1 match), I am using st_nearest_feature.
nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(thiessen_polygons, ohio_accidents_sf)
# 'nearest_idx' now gives, for each polygon, the index of the nearest accident point.

# and then I retrieve accident attribute data using these indices
accident_attributes <- ohio_accidents_sf[nearest_idx, ]

# After this I combine the accident attributes with the corresponding Voronoi polygon geometry.
# this will create my final polygon geometry service areas
thiessen_service_areas <- st_sf(accident_attributes, geometry = st_geometry(thiessen_polygons))

#  I then calculate the area of each service area in sq. km.
thiessen_service_areas$area_sq_km <- as.numeric(st_area(thiessen_service_areas)) / 1e6

# so I calculate basic stats for the service areas.
service_area_stats <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Minimum Area", "Maximum Area", "Mean Area", "Median Area", "Total Area"),
  Value_sq_km = c(
    min(thiessen_service_areas$area_sq_km),
    max(thiessen_service_areas$area_sq_km),
    mean(thiessen_service_areas$area_sq_km),
    median(thiessen_service_areas$area_sq_km),
    sum(thiessen_service_areas$area_sq_km)
  )
)

#— Load libraries
library(sf)
library(mapsf)
library(terra)
library(viridisLite)

#— 1. Reproject to geographic CRS (WGS84) for axes
thiessen_geo       <- st_transform(thiessen_service_areas, 4326)
ohio_boundary_geo  <- st_transform(ohio_boundary,          4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf,      4326)

#— 2. Build a template raster over Ohio at higher resolution (0.01°) for better quality
bbox     <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)  # Use Ohio boundary for complete coverage
template <- rast(
  xmin       = bbox["xmin"], xmax = bbox["xmax"],
  ymin       = bbox["ymin"], ymax = bbox["ymax"],
  resolution = 0.01,  # Higher resolution than before
  crs        = "EPSG:4326"
)

#— 3. Rasterize the Thiessen polygon areas
area_rast <- rasterize(
  vect(thiessen_geo),
  template,
  field = "area_sq_km"
)

#— 4. Plot setup: no margins around
par(mar = c(3,3,2,1))
plot(
  st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
  col    = NA,
  border = NA,
  axes   = FALSE,
  main   = paste0(
    "Pipeline Accident Service Areas in Ohio\n",
    "Thiessen Polygons by Size"
  ),
  cex.main = 1.2
)

#— 5. Add gridlines & lat/long labels
lon_br <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_br <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)
lon_lb <- paste0(abs(round(lon_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lon_br<0,"W","E"))
lat_lb <- paste0(abs(round(lat_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lat_br<0,"S","N"))
for (x in lon_br) abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lty = 2)
for (y in lat_br) abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lty = 2)

#— 6. Continuous raster layer with reversed plasma palette
mf_raster(
  x       = area_rast,
  pal     = viridisLite::plasma(100, direction = -1),
  nbreaks = 100,
  add     = TRUE,
  leg_pos = NA    # suppress default legend
)

#— 7. Custom continuous legend with ticks at 2000, 4000, 6000
mf_legend(
  type   = "cont",
  pos    = "right",
  title  = "Service Area (sq km)",
  val    = c(2000, 4000, 6000),
  pal    = viridisLite::plasma(100, direction = -1)
)

#— 8. Overlay polygon boundaries for sharpness
mf_map(
  x      = thiessen_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = NA,  # No fill, just boundaries
  border = "black",
  lwd    = 0.2,
  add    = TRUE
)

#— 9. Overlay boundary & accident locations
mf_map(
  x      = ohio_boundary_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = NA,
  border = "black",
  lwd    = 0.5,
  add    = TRUE
)
mf_map(
  x      = ohio_accidents_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = "red",
  pch    = 19,
  cex    = 0.6,
  add    = TRUE
)

#— 10. Add axes, north arrow, scale bar, and frame
axis(1, at = lon_br, labels = lon_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_br, labels = lat_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft")
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")
box()



print(service_area_stats)

```





```{r}
# I am trying to identify duplicate coordinates and adding a small jitter to make them unique
coords <- st_coordinates(ohio_accidents_sf)
dup_indices <- which(duplicated(coords) | duplicated(coords, fromLast = TRUE))

# I am creating  a copy of the accidents data that I can modify and avoid any overwriting
ohio_accidents_jittered <- ohio_accidents_sf

# so what I do here is I add a very small random offset to duplicated points (1m)
# this is only for creating Thiessen polygons not for analysis
if(length(dup_indices) > 0) {
  jitter_coords <- coords[dup_indices,]
  jitter_coords[,1] <- jitter_coords[,1] + runif(length(dup_indices), -1, 1)
  jitter_coords[,2] <- jitter_coords[,2] + runif(length(dup_indices), -1, 1)
  
  # and then I replace the coordinates of duplicated points
  jittered_points <- st_as_sf(as.data.frame(jitter_coords), 
                            coords = c("X", "Y"), 
                            crs = st_crs(ohio_accidents_sf))
  
  # and also I replace the geometries of duplicated points
  st_geometry(ohio_accidents_jittered)[dup_indices] <- st_geometry(jittered_points)
}


# I am using the st_voronoi function with jittered points
thiessen_geom <- st_voronoi(st_union(ohio_accidents_jittered))
thiessen_sf <- st_collection_extract(thiessen_geom) %>%
  st_intersection(st_union(ohio_boundary))

# then I convert to sf data frame to add unique IDs
thiessen_sf <- st_sf(geometry = thiessen_sf) %>%
  mutate(thiessen_id = row_number())

# and I find which accident point falls within which Thiessen polygon
point_polygon_match <- st_intersects(ohio_accidents_sf, thiessen_sf)

# here again I am creating a data frame linking accidents to Thiessen polygons
accident_thiessen_map <- data.frame(
  accident_index = 1:nrow(ohio_accidents_sf),
  thiessen_index = sapply(point_polygon_match, function(x) ifelse(length(x) > 0, x[1], NA))
)

# and also I remove records that are without a matching polygon 
accident_thiessen_map <- accident_thiessen_map[!is.na(accident_thiessen_map$thiessen_index),]

# here I am calculating the area of each Thiessen polygon
thiessen_sf$area_sq_km <- as.numeric(st_area(thiessen_sf)) / 1000000



# and also the calculate basic statistics for the Thiessen polygons
thiessen_stats <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Number of Thiessen Polygons", 
                "Minimum Area (sq km)", 
                "Maximum Area (sq km)", 
                "Mean Area (sq km)", 
                "Median Area (sq km)", 
                "Total Area (sq km)"),
  Value = c(
    nrow(thiessen_sf),
    min(thiessen_sf$area_sq_km),
    max(thiessen_sf$area_sq_km),
    mean(thiessen_sf$area_sq_km),
    median(thiessen_sf$area_sq_km),
    sum(thiessen_sf$area_sq_km)
  )
)

# Printing the statistics
print(thiessen_stats)
```

```{r}
# First, I create a grid over Ohio
ohio_grid <- st_make_grid(ohio_boundary, cellsize = 1000, square = TRUE) %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  st_intersection(ohio_boundary) %>%
  mutate(grid_id = row_number())

# For IDW, I need a value to interpolate for that 
# I am using a  simple binary presence (1) for accident points
ohio_accidents_sf$presence <- 1

# and then I check the required format for gstat::idw
str(ohio_grid)
```


```{r}
# I create a simplified grid 
ohio_grid_simple <- st_make_grid(ohio_boundary, cellsize = 5000, square = TRUE) %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  st_intersection(ohio_boundary) %>%
  mutate(grid_id = row_number())

# I first set up IDW interpolation so I can interpolate accident density rather than just presence
# First, I count accidents per 10km grid cell to get density values for interpolation
point_counts <- st_intersects(ohio_grid_simple, ohio_accidents_sf)
ohio_grid_simple$accident_count <- lengths(point_counts)
ohio_grid_simple$area_sqkm <- as.numeric(st_area(ohio_grid_simple)) / 1000000
ohio_grid_simple$accident_density <- ohio_grid_simple$accident_count / ohio_grid_simple$area_sqkm

# Then I create centroids of grid cells to use as base points for interpolation
ohio_grid_centroids <- st_centroid(ohio_grid_simple)

# and I create a regular grid for the IDW interpolation (prediction locations)
idw_grid <- st_make_grid(ohio_boundary, cellsize = 2500, square = TRUE) %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  st_intersection(ohio_boundary)

# then I convert to stars object for gstat
idw_grid_stars <- st_as_stars(idw_grid)

# Finally performing IDW interpolation
library(gstat)
idw_formula <- ohio_grid_centroids$accident_density ~ 1
idw_model <- gstat::idw(formula = idw_formula, 
                       locations = ohio_grid_centroids,
                       newdata = idw_grid_stars, 
                       idp = 2)  # idp is the power parameter (2 is standard)

# and then I convert to sf for plotting
idw_sf <- st_as_sf(idw_model)

# map
# Load necessary libraries
library(sf)
library(mapsf)

# Transform data to appropriate projection
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
idw_sf_geo <- st_transform(idw_sf, 4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)

# Define the quantile breaks that were missing
# This creates 5 breaks (for 4 intervals) based on quantiles
quant_breaks <- quantile(idw_sf_geo$var1.pred, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.25))

# Set up the plotting area
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 6))  # Adjusted margins to fit legend

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA, 
     border = NA,
     axes = FALSE,
     main = "Pipeline Accident Risk Surface in Ohio")

# Get the bounding box for grid lines
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)

# Create latitude and longitude breaks
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 2), "° W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}
for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Plot IDW data directly using a simple choropleth approach
# First, create a custom color palette matching your dens_pal
# Use the same colors as in your original plot
idw_colors <- c("#000080", "#800080", "#FF0080", "#FFA500", "#FFFF00")
n_breaks <- length(quant_breaks) - 1
idw_cols <- colorRampPalette(idw_colors)(n_breaks)

# Add IDW interpolation without white spaces
plot(st_geometry(idw_sf_geo), 
     col = idw_cols[findInterval(idw_sf_geo$var1.pred, quant_breaks)],
     border = NA,
     add = TRUE)

# Add Ohio boundary to clip edges
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "black",
     lwd = 0.5,
     add = TRUE)

# Plot accident points
plot(st_geometry(ohio_accidents_geo),
     col = "red",
     pch = 16,
     cex = 0.8,
     add = TRUE)

# Add subtitle
mtext("Inverse Distance Weighted (IDW) Interpolation of Accident Density",
      side = 3, line = -0.1, cex = 0.8)

# Add manual axes with lat/long labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# Add scale bar
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the plot area
box()

# Create a custom legend with proper decimal formatting
# Format breaks with 3 decimal places
legend_labels <- format(round(quant_breaks[-1], 3), nsmall = 3)
legend("right", 
       legend = legend_labels,
       fill = idw_cols,
       bty = "n",
       cex = 0.8,
       title = "Accident Density\n(per sq km)")

# I am trying to calcualte stats for the IDW interpolation
idw_stats <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Minimum Density", "Maximum Density", "Mean Density", "Median Density"),
  Value = c(
    min(idw_sf$var1.pred, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(idw_sf$var1.pred, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(idw_sf$var1.pred, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(idw_sf$var1.pred, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

# Printing the stats 
print(idw_stats)
```

```{r}
ohio_tracts_boundaries <- st_read("~/Assignment/cb_2019_39_tract_500k/cb_2019_39_tract_500k.shp")

# I am trying to check which objects exist with population data
exists("ohio_pop")
exists("total_ohio_pop")
exists("population_3km")

# and then I am creating a population estimate based on land area since I don't have actual census data due to server issue
ohio_tracts_boundaries$population <- as.numeric(ohio_tracts_boundaries$ALAND) / 1e6

# then I transform to match the CRS of my risk data
ohio_tracts_boundaries <- st_transform(ohio_tracts_boundaries, st_crs(idw_sf))

# Check if the population column was created successfully
head(ohio_tracts_boundaries$population)

# now first  I am trying to create a simpler risk area analysis without population
risk_threshold <- quantile(idw_sf$var1.pred, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
high_risk_areas <- idw_sf %>%
  dplyr::filter(var1.pred >= risk_threshold) %>%
  st_union() %>%
  st_sf()

mod_risk_threshold <- quantile(idw_sf$var1.pred, 0.70, na.rm = TRUE)
mod_risk_areas <- idw_sf %>%
  dplyr::filter(var1.pred >= mod_risk_threshold & var1.pred < risk_threshold) %>%
  st_union() %>%
  st_sf()

# then I calculate areas
high_risk_area <- sum(as.numeric(st_area(high_risk_areas))) / 1000000  # sq km
mod_risk_area <- sum(as.numeric(st_area(mod_risk_areas))) / 1000000    # sq km
ohio_area <- sum(as.numeric(st_area(ohio_boundary))) / 1000000         # sq km

# then I compile the list of  calculated risk areas 
risk_area_summary <- data.frame(
  Risk_Zone = c("High Risk", "Moderate Risk", "All of Ohio"),
  Area_Sq_Km = c(high_risk_area, mod_risk_area, ohio_area),
  Area_Percent = c(high_risk_area / ohio_area * 100,
                  mod_risk_area / ohio_area * 100,
                  100)
)

print("Risk Zone Area Statistics:")
print(risk_area_summary)

# Then I am calculating population density using my estimated population findings 
ohio_tracts_boundaries$pop_density <- ohio_tracts_boundaries$population / 
  (as.numeric(st_area(ohio_tracts_boundaries)) / 1000000)  # per sq km
```

```{r}
ls()[grep("populat|ohio_pop", ls())]

if(exists("population_3km")) {

library(tidycensus)
tryCatch({
  ohio_tracts_data <- get_acs(
    geography = "tract",
    variables = "B01003_001", 
    state = "OH",
    year = 2019,
    geometry = FALSE
  )
  
  # I am doing another join with  population data to the boundary file
  ohio_tracts_boundaries$estimate <- ohio_tracts_data$estimate[match(ohio_tracts_boundaries$GEOID, ohio_tracts_data$GEOID)]
  
  # map

library(mapsf)
library(viridisLite)

# First calculate population density for the tracts
# This assumes ohio_tracts_sf already has the 'estimate' column for population
ohio_tracts_sf$pop_density <- ohio_tracts_sf$estimate / as.numeric(st_area(ohio_tracts_sf)) * 1000000

# Transform everything to WGS84 for consistent coordinate display
ohio_tracts_geo <- st_transform(ohio_tracts_sf, 4326)
high_risk_areas_geo <- st_transform(high_risk_areas, 4326)
mod_risk_areas_geo <- st_transform(mod_risk_areas, 4326)
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)

# Compute gridlines & labels
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)
lon_br <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_br <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)
lon_lb <- paste0(abs(round(lon_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lon_br<0,"W","E"))
lat_lb <- paste0(abs(round(lat_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lat_br<0,"N","N"))

# Set up the plot with margins for the legend
# Increase top margin to allow space for title and subtitle
par(mar = c(3,3,3,6))  # Increased top margin from 2 to 3

# Draw base map with title and grid
plot(
  st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
  col = NA,
  border = NA,
  axes = FALSE,
  main = "Population Exposure to Pipeline Accident Risk in Ohio",
  cex.main = 1.2
)

# Add subtitle with more space below the main title
mtext("Area-weighted interpolation of population in high and moderate risk zones", 
      side = 3, line = 0.3, cex = 0.8)  # Increased line from 0.2 to 0.8

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_br) abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lty = 2)
for(y in lat_br) abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lty = 2)

# Create logarithmic breaks for population density
# Get min/max values, skipping any zero or NA values
min_density <- min(ohio_tracts_geo$pop_density[ohio_tracts_geo$pop_density > 0], na.rm = TRUE)
max_density <- max(ohio_tracts_geo$pop_density, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create breaks that match the ggplot example (approximately)
# Using powers of 10 for better readability
log_breaks <- c(5, 19, 68, 243, 876, 3153, 11348)

# Create matching color palette - using the plasma palette in reverse
# to match the viridis colormap in the ggplot example
viridis_pal <- viridisLite::viridis(100, option = "viridis")
dens_pal <- viridis_pal[seq(1, 100, length.out = length(log_breaks) - 1)]

# Plot population density
mf_map(
  x = ohio_tracts_geo,
  var = "pop_density",
  type = "choro",
  breaks = log_breaks,
  pal = dens_pal,
  border = NA,
  add = TRUE,
  leg_pos = NA
)

# Add risk zones with increased transparency
# Use more transparent colors for risk areas
mf_map(
  x = mod_risk_areas_geo,
  type = "base",
  col = adjustcolor("#FFA500", alpha.f = 0.5),  # orange with more transparency
  border = adjustcolor("#FFA500", alpha.f = 0.7),
  lwd = 0.5,
  add = TRUE
)

mf_map(
  x = high_risk_areas_geo,
  type = "base",
  col = adjustcolor("#FF0000", alpha.f = 0.5),  # red with more transparency 
  border = adjustcolor("#FF0000", alpha.f = 0.7),
  lwd = 0.5,
  add = TRUE
)

# Add Ohio boundary
mf_map(
  x = ohio_boundary_geo,
  type = "base",
  col = NA,
  border = "black",
  lwd = 0.5,
  add = TRUE
)

# Add axes with labels
axis(1, at = lon_br, labels = lon_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_br, labels = lat_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow and scale bar
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft")
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the map
box()

# Add legend for population density on the right
mf_legend(
  type = "choro",
  title = "Population\nDensity\n(per sq km)",
  val = log_breaks,
  pal = dens_pal,
  pos = "right",
  frame = TRUE
)

# Add legend for risk zones at bottom right
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("High Risk", "Moderate Risk"),
  fill = c(adjustcolor("#FF0000", alpha.f = 0.5), adjustcolor("#FFA500", alpha.f = 0.5)),
  border = c(adjustcolor("#FF0000", alpha.f = 0.7), adjustcolor("#FFA500", alpha.f = 0.7)),
  box.lty = 1,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

# Load necessary libraries
library(sf)
library(mapsf)

# Transform data to geographic CRS (WGS84) for lat/long display
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)

# Set up the plotting area
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA, 
     border = NA,
     axes = FALSE,
     main = "Pipeline Accidents in Ohio by Incident Type")

# Get the bounding box for grid lines
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)

# Create latitude and longitude breaks
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 2), "° W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Add Ohio fill
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = "white",
     border = NA,
     add = TRUE)

# Define colors for different incident types
# Get unique incident types
incident_types <- unique(ohio_accidents_geo$Incident.Type)
incident_colors <- c("hazardous" = "red", 
                     "distribution" = "blue", 
                     "transmission" = "green",
                     "gathering" = "purple",
                     "other" = "orange")

# For any incident types not in our predefined list, assign "grey"
for(type in incident_types) {
  if(!type %in% names(incident_colors)) {
    incident_colors[type] <- "grey"
  }
}

# Create a color vector based on incident types
point_colors <- incident_colors[ohio_accidents_geo$Incident.Type]

# Plot accident points colored by incident type
plot(st_geometry(ohio_accidents_geo),
     col = point_colors,
     pch = 16,
     cex = 1,
     add = TRUE)

# Add Ohio boundary to clean/clip edges
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "black",
     add = TRUE)

# Add manual axes with lat/long labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# Add scale bar
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the plot area
box()

# Add legend for incident types
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = names(incident_colors),
       col = incident_colors,
       pch = 16,
       bty = "n",
       cex = 0.8,
       title = "Incident Type")
```

```{r}
# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

# Buffer Analysis for Exposure Zones
# Create larger buffers for better visualization
# Scaling up the buffer distances while maintaining their relative proportions
buffer_500m <- st_buffer(ohio_accidents_sf, 5000)  # 10x larger for visibility
buffer_1km <- st_buffer(ohio_accidents_sf, 10000)  # 10x larger for visibility
buffer_3km <- st_buffer(ohio_accidents_sf, 30000)  # 10x larger for visibility

# Transform data to geographic CRS (WGS84) for lat/long display
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)

# Set up the plotting area
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),

lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

}

# Add Ohio fill

# Plot buffer zones first (BEFORE accident points)

# 1km zone (orange) - now much larger

# 500m zone (red) - now much larger

# Add Ohio boundary to clean/clip edges

# Update subtitle to explain the scaling

axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
```

```{r}
# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

# Transform data to geographic CRS (WGS84) for lat/long display
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)
std_circle_geo <- st_transform(std_circle, 4326)

# Transform mean center and calculate axes in geographic coordinates
mean_center_geo <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(ohio_accidents_geo)))

# Transform the axes calculations to geographic space
# Get the original angle and distances
coords_geo <- st_coordinates(ohio_accidents_geo)
cov_matrix_geo <- cov(coords_geo)
eigen_result_geo <- eigen(cov_matrix_geo)
eigen_vectors_geo <- eigen_result_geo$vectors
eigen_values_geo <- eigen_result_geo$values
angle_geo <- atan2(eigen_vectors_geo[2,1], eigen_vectors_geo[1,1])

# Calculate major and minor axes in geographic coordinates
major_axis_geo <- sqrt(eigen_values_geo[1]) * 2
minor_axis_geo <- sqrt(eigen_values_geo[2]) * 2

# Set up the plotting area
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA, 
     border = NA,
     axes = FALSE,
     main = "Directional Distribution of Pipeline Accidents in Ohio")

# Get the bounding box for grid lines
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)

# Create latitude and longitude breaks
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 2), "° W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}
for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Add Ohio fill
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = "white",
     border = NA,
     add = TRUE)

# Plot the standard distance circle
plot(st_geometry(std_circle_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "blue",
     lwd = 1,
     add = TRUE)

# Add the major axis arrow
arrows(
  mean_center_geo[1], mean_center_geo[2],
  mean_center_geo[1] + cos(angle_geo) * major_axis_geo,
  mean_center_geo[2] + sin(angle_geo) * major_axis_geo,
  col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, length = 0.10
)

# Add the minor axis arrow
arrows(
  mean_center_geo[1], mean_center_geo[2],
  mean_center_geo[1] + cos(angle_geo + pi/2) * minor_axis_geo,
  mean_center_geo[2] + sin(angle_geo + pi/2) * minor_axis_geo,
  col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, length = 0.10
)

# Add Ohio boundary
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "black",
     lwd = 0.5,
     add = TRUE)

# Plot the accident points
plot(st_geometry(ohio_accidents_geo),
     col = "red",
     pch = 16,
     cex = 1.5,
     add = TRUE)

# Add subtitle
mtext("Mean Center, Standard Distance, and Principal Axes",
      side = 3, line = -0.1, cex = 0.8)

# Add manual axes with lat/long labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# Add scale bar
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the plot area
box()

# Add a custom legend
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c("Accident Locations", "Standard Distance", "Major Axis", "Minor Axis"),
       col = c("red", "blue", "darkblue", "darkgreen"),
       pch = c(16, NA, NA, NA),
       lty = c(NA, 1, 1, 1),
       lwd = c(NA, 1, 2, 2),
       pt.cex = 1.5,
       bty = "n",
       cex = 0.8,
       title = "Map Elements")
```
