```{r}
# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

library(sf)
library(spatstat)   # for ppp & density.ppp
library(sp)         # for CRS()/proj4string()
library(terra)      # for SpatRaster
library(mapsf)      # for the mapping functions
library(raster)     # for raster operations

# 1) build the point pattern & 5 km KDE in UTM --------------------------------
ohio_utm     <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 26917)
ohio_acc_utm <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 26917)
ohio_win <- as.owin(st_geometry(ohio_utm))
coords   <- st_coordinates(ohio_acc_utm)
suppressWarnings({
  ohio_ppp <- ppp(coords[,1], coords[,2], window = ohio_win, check = FALSE)
})
ohio_density <- density.ppp(ohio_ppp, sigma = 5000, edge = TRUE)

# 2) get back to geographic for sf plotting ----------------------------------
ohio_bound_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
ohio_acc_geo   <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)

# 3) convert the KDE ("im" object) into a terra SpatRaster -------------------
sgdf <- as(ohio_density, "SpatialGridDataFrame")
proj4string(sgdf) <- st_crs(26917)$proj4string   # tell it "this is UTM"

# Convert to a raster object (raster package) for better control
r <- raster(sgdf)

# Apply log transformation to match the reference map
r_log <- calc(r, fun = function(x) log10(x * 100 + 1))

# Project to WGS84
r_wgs84 <- projectRaster(r_log, crs = st_crs(4326)$proj4string)

# Create a mask from Ohio to constrain the KDE display
ohio_sp <- as(ohio_bound_geo, "Spatial")
r_masked <- mask(r_wgs84, ohio_sp)

# 4) colour ramp --------------------------------------------------------------
density_cols <- colorRampPalette(
  c("navy", "blue", "purple", "red", "orange", "yellow")
)(100)

# 5) draw the map with base R for better control -----------------------------
# Set margins to match reference
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 6))  # room for right-hand legend & title

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_bound_geo),
     col = NA, 
     border = NA,
     axes = FALSE,
     main = "")

# Get the bounding box for grid lines
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_bound_geo)

# Create latitude and longitude breaks
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 1), "°W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 1), "°N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}
for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Fill Ohio with white as the base layer
plot(st_geometry(ohio_bound_geo),
     col = "white",
     border = NA,
     add = TRUE)

# Plot the masked raster directly - the simpler approach that works
plot(r_masked, 
     col = density_cols, 
     add = TRUE, 
     legend = FALSE)

# Add Ohio boundary again with a clean black line
plot(st_geometry(ohio_bound_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "black",
     lwd = 1,
     add = TRUE)

# Add accident points
plot(st_geometry(ohio_acc_geo),
     col = "red",
     pch = 16,
     cex = 0.7,
     add = TRUE)

# Add title and subtitle separately for better control
title("Kernel Density of Pipeline Accidents in Ohio", cex.main = 1.2)
mtext("Smoothed with 5km Gaussian Kernel (log scale)", 
      side = 3, line = -0.1, cex = 0.8)

# Add axes with lat/long labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow (using mapsf)
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# Add scale bar (using mapsf)
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the plot area
box()

# Create the tick-style legend
par(xpd = TRUE)  # Allow plotting outside the plot region

# Calculate legend position based on the plot dimensions
usr <- par("usr")  # Get the plot region coordinates
legend_x <- usr[2] + 0.05 * (usr[2] - usr[1])
legend_y_bottom <- usr[3] + 0.25 * (usr[4] - usr[3])
legend_y_top <- usr[3] + 0.75 * (usr[4] - usr[3])
legend_width <- 0.02 * (usr[2] - usr[1])

# Draw the legend color bar
y_positions <- seq(legend_y_bottom, legend_y_top, length.out = 101)
for (i in 1:100) {
  rect(legend_x, y_positions[i], legend_x + legend_width, y_positions[i+1],
       col = density_cols[i], border = NA)
}

# Add a border around the color bar
rect(legend_x, legend_y_bottom, legend_x + legend_width, legend_y_top, 
     col = NULL, border = "black")

# Create custom legend labels
tick_positions <- seq(legend_y_bottom, legend_y_top, length.out = 5)
tick_labels <- c("0.0", "", "0.1", "", "0.3")  # Values from the reference image

# Draw tick marks and labels
segments(legend_x + legend_width, tick_positions, 
         legend_x + legend_width + 0.01 * (usr[2] - usr[1]), tick_positions)
text(legend_x + legend_width + 0.015 * (usr[2] - usr[1]), 
     tick_positions, tick_labels, adj = 0, cex = 0.7)

# Add legend title
text(legend_x + legend_width/2, legend_y_top + 0.05 * (usr[4] - usr[3]), 
     "KDE\n(log scale)", adj = c(0.5, 0), cex = 0.8)

par(xpd = FALSE)  # Reset to not plot outside the plot region
```

# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

library(sf)
library(mapsf)
library(viridisLite)
library(dplyr)
library(forcats)

#— 1. Make sure your sf object has that sensitivity factor,
#     and convert ANY remaining NAs into "Unknown":
ohio_accidents_sf <- ohio_accidents_sf %>%
  mutate(
    sensitivity = fct_explicit_na(
      sensitivity,
      na_level = "Unknown"
    )
  )

#— 2. Reproject everything to your chosen CRS
ohio_boundary_geo   <- st_transform(ohio_boundary,       26917)
nhd_waterbodies_geo <- st_transform(nhd_waterbodies_ohio,26917)
nhd_flowline_geo    <- st_transform(nhd_flowline_ohio,   26917)
ohio_accidents_geo  <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf,   26917)

#— 3. Create a palette *including* "Unknown" at the end
base_levels <- c("Very Low","Low","Medium","High","Very High")
pal_vals <- viridis(5, option = "D", direction = -1)
palette_vals <- c(setNames(pal_vals, base_levels),
                  "Unknown" = "gray50")

#— 4. Tight margins
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))

#— 5. Empty base map + title
plot(
  st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
  col      = NA,
  border   = NA,
  axes     = FALSE,
  main     = paste0(
               "Pipeline Accidents by Environmental Sensitivity in Ohio\n",
               "Classification based on land use type sensitivity"
             ),
  cex.main = 0.8
)

#— 6. Gridlines & labels
bbox       <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)
lon_labels <- paste0(abs(round(lon_breaks,2)), "°", ifelse(lon_breaks<0,"W","E"))
lat_labels <- paste0(abs(round(lat_breaks,2)), "°", ifelse(lat_breaks<0,"S","N"))
for (x in lon_breaks) abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lty = 2)
for (y in lat_breaks) abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lty = 2)

#— 7. Draw water & flowlines
mf_map(nhd_waterbodies_geo, type = "base", col = "lightblue", border = NA, add = TRUE)
mf_map(nhd_flowline_geo,    type = "base", col = "blue",      lwd    = 1,  add = TRUE)

#— 8. Plot accident points (typology), suppressing mf_map’s legend
mf_map(
  ohio_accidents_geo,
  type    = "typo",
  var     = "sensitivity",
  pal     = palette_vals,
  pch     = 19,
  cex     = 0.9,
  add     = TRUE,
  leg_pos = NA
)

#— 9. Now draw a clean categorical legend with *exactly* your 6 levels
mf_legend(
  type  = "typo",
  pos   = "right",
  val   = names(palette_vals),
  pal   = palette_vals,
  title = "Environmental\nSensitivity"
)

#— 10. Overlay the state border
mf_map(
  ohio_boundary_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = NA,
  border = "black",
  lwd    = 1,
  add    = TRUE
)

#— 11. Axes, arrow, scale, box
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft")
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")
box()

# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

library(sf)
library(mapsf)
library(viridisLite)

# 1) Reproject everything to WGS84 so axes are in °N/°W
ohio_counties_geo <- st_transform(ohio_counties_sf, 4326)
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)

# 2) Compute your gridlines & labels once
bbox    <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)
lon_br  <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_br  <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)
lon_lb  <- paste0(abs(round(lon_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lon_br<0,"W","E"))
lat_lb  <- paste0(abs(round(lat_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lat_br<0,"N","N"))

# 3) Shared Plasma palette
pal100 <- viridisLite::plasma(100, direction = -1)

# 4) Helper to draw the blank base + grids + title
draw_base <- function(title) {
  par(mar = c(3,3,2,1))
  plot(
    st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
    col    = NA,
    border = NA,
    axes   = FALSE,
    main   = title,
    cex.main = 1.2
  )
  for(x in lon_br) abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lty = 2)
  for(y in lat_br) abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lty = 2)
}

# 5) Helper to overlay boundary, axes, arrow, scale & box
add_axes <- function() {
  mf_map(
    x      = ohio_boundary_geo,
    type   = "base",
    col    = NA,
    border = "black",
    add    = TRUE
  )
  axis(1, at = lon_br, labels = lon_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
  axis(2, at = lat_br, labels = lat_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
  mf_arrow(pos = "topleft")
  mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")
  box()
}

#–– Map 1: Accident counts ––
draw_base("Pipeline Accidents by County in Ohio")

# Create quantile breaks for accident count - fixed approach
count_values <- ohio_counties_geo$accident_count
# For quantiles, we'll use the stats::quantile function
count_breaks <- c(
  0,  # start at 0
  stats::quantile(
    count_values[count_values > 0],  # skip zeros for better breaks
    probs = seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.2)
  ),
  max(count_values)  # end at max value
)

# Create a custom color palette with 7 colors (for 6 intervals)
count_pal <- pal100[seq(1, 100, length.out = length(count_breaks) - 1)]

mf_map(
  x        = ohio_counties_geo,
  type     = "choro",
  var      = "accident_count",
  breaks   = count_breaks,
  pal      = count_pal,
  border   = "grey70",
  lwd      = 0.4,
  add      = TRUE,
  leg_pos  = NA
)

# Custom legend
mf_legend(
  type   = "choro",
  pos    = "right",
  title  = "Number of\nAccidents",
  val    = count_breaks,
  pal    = count_pal,
  frame  = TRUE
)
add_axes()

#–– Map 2: Accident rate per 1000 km² ––
draw_base("Pipeline Accident Rate by County in Ohio")

# Create quantile breaks for accident rate
rate_values <- ohio_counties_geo$accident_rate
rate_breaks <- c(
  0,  # start at 0
  stats::quantile(
    rate_values[rate_values > 0],  # skip zeros for better breaks
    probs = seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.2)
  ),
  max(rate_values)  # end at max value
)

# Create a custom color palette
rate_pal <- pal100[seq(1, 100, length.out = length(rate_breaks) - 1)]

mf_map(
  x        = ohio_counties_geo,
  type     = "choro",
  var      = "accident_rate",
  breaks   = rate_breaks,
  pal      = rate_pal,
  border   = "grey70",
  lwd      = 0.4,
  add      = TRUE,
  leg_pos  = NA
)

mf_legend(
  type   = "choro",
  pos    = "right",
  title  = "Accidents per\n1000 sq km",
  val    = rate_breaks,
  pal    = rate_pal,
  frame  = TRUE
)
add_axes()

#–– Map 3: Population-weighted risk per 100,000 people ––

# Create quantile breaks for population risk

```{r}
# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

#— Load libraries
library(sf)
library(mapsf)
library(terra)
library(viridisLite)

#— 1. Reproject to geographic CRS (WGS84) for axes
thiessen_geo       <- st_transform(thiessen_service_areas, 4326)
ohio_boundary_geo  <- st_transform(ohio_boundary,          4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf,      4326)

#— 2. Build a template raster over Ohio at higher resolution (0.01°) for better quality
bbox     <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)  # Use Ohio boundary for complete coverage
template <- rast(
  xmin       = bbox["xmin"], xmax = bbox["xmax"],
  ymin       = bbox["ymin"], ymax = bbox["ymax"],
  resolution = 0.01,  # Higher resolution than before
  crs        = "EPSG:4326"
)

#— 3. Rasterize the Thiessen polygon areas
area_rast <- rasterize(
  vect(thiessen_geo),
  template,
  field = "area_sq_km"
)

#— 4. Plot setup: no margins around
par(mar = c(3,3,2,1))
plot(
  st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
  col    = NA,
  border = NA,
  axes   = FALSE,
  main   = paste0(
    "Pipeline Accident Service Areas in Ohio\n",
    "Thiessen Polygons by Size"
  ),
  cex.main = 1.2
)

#— 5. Add gridlines & lat/long labels
lon_br <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_br <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)
lon_lb <- paste0(abs(round(lon_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lon_br<0,"W","E"))
lat_lb <- paste0(abs(round(lat_br,2)), "°", ifelse(lat_br<0,"S","N"))
for (x in lon_br) abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lty = 2)
for (y in lat_br) abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lty = 2)

#— 6. Continuous raster layer with reversed plasma palette
mf_raster(
  x       = area_rast,
  pal     = viridisLite::plasma(100, direction = -1),
  nbreaks = 100,
  add     = TRUE,
  leg_pos = NA    # suppress default legend
)

#— 7. Custom continuous legend with ticks at 2000, 4000, 6000
mf_legend(
  type   = "cont",
  pos    = "right",
  title  = "Service Area (sq km)",
  val    = c(2000, 4000, 6000),
  pal    = viridisLite::plasma(100, direction = -1)
)

#— 8. Overlay polygon boundaries for sharpness
mf_map(
  x      = thiessen_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = NA,  # No fill, just boundaries
  border = "black",
  lwd    = 0.2,
  add    = TRUE
)

#— 9. Overlay boundary & accident locations
mf_map(
  x      = ohio_boundary_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = NA,
  border = "black",
  lwd    = 0.5,
  add    = TRUE
)
mf_map(
  x      = ohio_accidents_geo,
  type   = "base",
  col    = "red",
  pch    = 19,
  cex    = 0.6,
  add    = TRUE
)

#— 10. Add axes, north arrow, scale bar, and frame
axis(1, at = lon_br, labels = lon_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_br, labels = lat_lb, cex.axis = 0.7)
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft")
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")
box()

```

# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

# Create a summary data frame for commodity analysis
commodity_summary <- data.frame(
  Commodity = names(sort(table(ohio_accidents_sf$Commodity), decreasing = TRUE)),
  Count = as.numeric(sort(table(ohio_accidents_sf$Commodity), decreasing = TRUE)),
  Percentage = as.numeric(sort(table(ohio_accidents_sf$Commodity), decreasing = TRUE)) / nrow(ohio_accidents_sf) * 100
)

# Add a more generalized classification
commodity_summary$Category <- "Other"
commodity_summary$Category[commodity_summary$Commodity %in% c("OIL", "GASOLINE", "DIESEL", "JET FUEL")] <- "Refined Petroleum"
commodity_summary$Category[commodity_summary$Commodity %in% c("NATURAL GAS LIQUID", "LIQUIFIED GASES", "PROPANE")] <- "Gas/LNG"
commodity_summary$Category[commodity_summary$Commodity == ""] <- "Unknown"

# Add the commodity type to our accidents data for mapping
ohio_accidents_sf$commodity_category <- "Other"
ohio_accidents_sf$commodity_category[ohio_accidents_sf$Commodity %in% c("OIL", "GASOLINE", "DIESEL", "JET FUEL")] <- "Refined Petroleum"
ohio_accidents_sf$commodity_category[ohio_accidents_sf$Commodity %in% c("NATURAL GAS LIQUID", "LIQUIFIED GASES", "PROPANE")] <- "Gas/LNG"
ohio_accidents_sf$commodity_category[ohio_accidents_sf$Commodity == ""] <- "Unknown"

# Create a bar chart of commodity types
# Transform to geographic coordinates for mapping
ohio_boundary_geo <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 4326)
ohio_accidents_geo <- st_transform(ohio_accidents_sf, 4326)

# Set up the plotting area for the bar chart
par(mar = c(6, 8, 2, 2))

# Filter out empty commodity values for the plot
commodity_plot <- commodity_summary[commodity_summary$Commodity != "", ]

# Create barplot with commodity types
barplot(commodity_plot$Count,
        names.arg = commodity_plot$Commodity,
        horiz = TRUE,
        col = "steelblue",
        las = 1,
        cex.names = 0.8,
        main = "Pipeline Accidents by Commodity Type in Ohio",
        xlab = "Number of Accidents")

# Add percentages as text
text(commodity_plot$Count + max(commodity_plot$Count)/20, 
     seq(1.5, by = 1.2, length.out = nrow(commodity_plot)) - 0.5,
     paste0(round(commodity_plot$Percentage, 1), "%"),
     cex = 0.7)

# Create a map showing accidents by commodity type
# Reset plotting parameters
par(mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))

# Create empty plot with Ohio's extent
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA, 
     border = NA,
     axes = FALSE,
     main = "Pipeline Accidents by Commodity Type in Ohio")

# Get the bounding box for grid lines
bbox <- st_bbox(ohio_boundary_geo)

# Create latitude and longitude breaks
lon_breaks <- seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], length.out = 5)
lat_breaks <- seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], length.out = 5)

# Format lat/long labels
lon_labels <- paste0(round(lon_breaks, 2), "° W")
lat_labels <- paste0(round(lat_breaks, 2), "° N")

# Add grid lines
for(x in lon_breaks) {
  abline(v = x, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

for(y in lat_breaks) {
  abline(h = y, col = "grey90", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2)
}

# Add Ohio fill
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = "white",
     border = NA,
     add = TRUE)

# Create colors for commodity categories
commodity_colors <- c("Refined Petroleum" = "red", "Gas/LNG" = "blue", "Unknown" = "gray", "Other" = "green")

# Assign colors based on commodity categories
point_colors <- commodity_colors[ohio_accidents_geo$commodity_category]

# Plot accident points colored by commodity
plot(st_geometry(ohio_accidents_geo),
     col = point_colors,
     pch = 16,
     cex = 1,
     add = TRUE)

# Add Ohio boundary
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_geo),
     col = NA,
     border = "black",
     add = TRUE)

# Add manual axes with lat/long labels
axis(1, at = lon_breaks, labels = lon_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = lat_breaks, labels = lat_labels, cex.axis = 0.7)

# Add north arrow
mf_arrow(pos = "topleft", col = "black")

# Add scale bar
mf_scale(pos = "bottomleft")

# Add box around the plot area
box()

# Add legend
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = names(commodity_colors),
       col = commodity_colors,
       pch = 16,
       bty = "n",
       cex = 0.8,
       title = "Commodity Type")

# Temporal analysis - Look at commodity types over time
# Set up the plotting area
par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

# Create a heatmap-style visualization of commodity types by decade
decade_commodity <- table(ohio_accidents_sf$Decade, ohio_accidents_sf$Commodity)

# Calculate the percentage within each decade
decade_commodity_pct <- prop.table(decade_commodity, margin = 1) * 100

# Convert to data frame for plotting
decade_commodity_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(decade_commodity)
decade_commodity_pct_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(decade_commodity_pct)

# Print the results
print("Commodity types by decade (count):")
print(decade_commodity)

print("Commodity types by decade (percentage within decade):")
print(round(decade_commodity_pct, 1))

# Calculate average age of pipeline by commodity type
avg_age_by_commodity <- aggregate(Age..yrs. ~ Commodity, 
                                 data = st_drop_geometry(ohio_accidents_sf), 
                                 FUN = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))

# Order by average age
avg_age_by_commodity <- avg_age_by_commodity[order(-avg_age_by_commodity$Age..yrs.), ]

# Print the results
print("Average pipeline age at time of accident by commodity type:")
print(avg_age_by_commodity)

# I created this map to explore the spatial patterns in the data.

library(sf)
library(terra)
library(FedData)

ohio_boundary <- states(cb = TRUE, year = 2021) %>%
  dplyr::filter(STUSPS == "OH") %>%  # fully qualified
  st_transform(4326)



# 2. Download NLCD land‑cover raster for 2016 via FedData API
nlcd_api_raster <- get_nlcd(
  template       = ohio_boundary,
  year           = 2016,
  dataset        = "landcover",
  label          = "nlcd_api_ohio",
  extraction.dir = "~/Assignment/nlcd_api_download",
  force.redo     = FALSE
)

# 3. Reproject the raster to NAD83 / UTM zone 17N (EPSG:26917)
nlcd_26917 <- project(nlcd_api_raster, "EPSG:26917")

# 4. Reproject Ohio boundary to EPSG:26917
ohio_boundary_26917 <- st_transform(ohio_boundary, 26917)

# 5. Convert the boundary to a terra SpatVector for masking
ohio_vect_26917 <- vect(ohio_boundary_26917)

# 6. Crop and mask the reprojected raster to the Ohio extent
nlcd_clipped <- crop(nlcd_26917, ohio_vect_26917)
nlcd_clipped <- mask(nlcd_clipped, ohio_vect_26917)

# 7. Plot without axes or box
plot(nlcd_clipped,
     main = "Classified Land Cover Land Use Map of Ohio",
     axes = FALSE)          # suppress axes and box
plot(st_geometry(ohio_boundary_26917),
     add    = TRUE,
     border = "black")     # overlay the state boundary
